questions.question: What did the BLIMP paper report about sensitivity to the overall scale of the seismic data?
required_facts: BLIMP is completely insensitive to the overall scale of the seismic data, while recursion is not.
forbidden_claims: BLIMP is sensitive to the overall scale of the seismic data.
supporting_excerpts: Additionally, the BLIMP procedure is completely insensitive to the overall scale of the seismic data while recursion is not.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against 1996-21.pdf physical page 7 and parsed chunk geo-1996-21_22. The statement directly contrasts BLIMP with recursion.
questions.overlap_check: Separate from older BLIMP questions about the algorithm name, workflow, pre-frequency operation, or step 3.

questions.question: In the Nebraska CSP results, how much of the 23-mile dataset showed continuous definable reflectors likely classified as bedrock and matched with geologic logs?
required_facts: Approximately 23 percent, or 5 miles, of the data had continuous definable reflectors likely classified as bedrock that correlated with geologic logs.
forbidden_claims: All 23 miles showed continuous bedrock reflectors.
supporting_excerpts: Continuous definable reflectors likely classified as bedrock are present in approximately 23 percent (5 miles) of the data and are correlated with geologic logs.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against fs11503.pdf physical page 6 and parsed chunk geo-fs11503_38. This is a result statistic, separate from older questions about CSP purpose, signal, system sweep, velocity, and canal operations.
questions.overlap_check: No prior generation, Acceptance, or retrieval-dev question asks for the 23-percent/5-mile bedrock-reflector result.

questions.question: During the New River survey, how frequently were navigation fix marks automatically placed on the seismic records?
required_facts: Navigation fix marks were automatically placed on the seismic records generally every 60 seconds.
forbidden_claims: Navigation fix marks were placed every 400 milliseconds.
supporting_excerpts: Navigation fix marks were automatically placed on the seismic records generally every 60 seconds.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against report.pdf physical page 16 and parsed chunk geo-report-1989-4195_52.
questions.overlap_check: Distinct from earlier New River questions about survey purpose, navigation systems, filtering choice, velocity, or lithologic limits.

questions.question: What uncertainty in refraction velocity did the SH-wave paper estimate from sensitivity analysis of first-break picking?
required_facts: The estimated uncertainty was a plus-or-minus 10 percent error in refraction velocity measurements.
forbidden_claims: The estimated uncertainty was plus or minus 10 meters per second.
supporting_excerpts: Williams et al. estimated that a plus-or-minus 10 percent error on refraction velocity measurements is possible based on sensitivity analysis of refraction first-break picking.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against s10950-021-10042-z.pdf physical page 4 and parsed chunk geo-s10950-021-10042-z_28.
questions.overlap_check: Separate from earlier SH-wave questions about velocity reversals, blind zones, and the St. Louis geophone setup.

questions.question: According to the New River report, what components are required for continuous seismic profiling, and what raw recording is usually retained for later analysis?
required_facts: Continuous seismic profiling requires a rapid-pulse sound source, hydrophone or streamer cable, signal processor, and graphic recorder.
Magnetic tape of the raw, unfiltered signal is usually retained for subsequent analysis.
forbidden_claims: Only a navigation receiver and a graphic recorder are required.
supporting_excerpts: Continuous seismic profiling requires a rapid-pulse sound source, hydrophones or a streamer cable, a signal processor to amplify and filter signals, and a graphic recorder to record and display signals. A magnetic tape recording of the raw, unfiltered signal is usually made for subsequent analysis.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against report.pdf physical page 14 and parsed chunk geo-report-1989-4195_47. The source lists all four components and the retained raw recording in one evidence unit.
questions.overlap_check: Not a rewording of the prior New River survey-purpose, navigation, filter-choice, average-velocity, or lithology-limit questions.

questions.question: Where along Lines A and B did the Presidio report locate the low-velocity zones, and what overall feature orientation did those locations suggest?
required_facts: The low-velocity zone was at about 385 to 470 feet downline on Line A and about 375 to 415 feet downline on Line B.
Those locations suggested a feature trending approximately north-northwest across the site.
forbidden_claims: The feature trended east-west across the site.
supporting_excerpts: Low-velocity zones were identified at 385 to 470 feet downline on Line A and 375 to 415 feet downline on Line B. These locations suggest a feature trending approximately north-northwest across the site.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Checked against OF12-1191.pdf physical page 14 and parsed chunks geo-of12-1191_61 and geo-of12-1191_62; chunk _63 repeats part of the orientation and is equivalent backup evidence.
questions.overlap_check: Separate from earlier Presidio questions about geophone spread, rippable depths, tomography conclusion, and traveltime slopes.

questions.question: Under a technical-report-only filter, what sweep rate, firing rate, and power setting were used for most of the New River survey?
questions.manual_scope_note: The exact New River settings are on report.pdf physical page 16: 200-ms sweep, 400-ms repetition, and 280 joules. Its manifest type is report, so the technical-report-only filter excludes it. The only technical report is fs11503.pdf; it documents a different Nebraska system (2 to 10 kHz, four times per second) and cannot support New River settings.
questions.manual_evidence_note: Manually checked the manifest, New River report physical page 16, and the technical-report-only scope. The requested facts are unavailable inside the filter and must be refused.
questions.overlap_check: New refusal boundary: this tests a type-filter exclusion for a source that contains the requested facts outside the allowed scope.

questions.question: What exact fuel consumption, in gallons, did the New River seismic survey use over its four-day field campaign?
questions.manual_scope_note: Reviewed the New River report's abstract, methods, equipment, and field-survey pages and searched the six-document corpus for fuel, diesel, gasoline, gallon, and gallons. The only gallons occurrence in the New River report is on physical page 7 (chunk geo-report-1989-4195_16): 7.5 million gallons per day of Camp Lejeune ground-water withdrawals. It is not survey fuel consumption. No source gives a fuel-consumption total for the four-day survey.
questions.manual_evidence_note: The filtered report includes an unrelated groundwater-withdrawal quantity but no exact survey fuel figure. It would be unsupported to infer fuel use from that water-withdrawal statement.
questions.overlap_check: New corpus-insufficiency topic, not a simple rewrite of the existing exact survey-cost, maintenance, kWh, or 72-hour refusal questions.
